text:
I need an email to win back customers who cancelled. I own a home cleaning company with 18 cleaners.

What's true:
- We have 212 regular customers. 64 cancelled in the last year. In exit surveys, the most common reason was price, then a different cleaner showing up each time.
- An every-other-week cleaning for a 3-bedroom house costs $165 with us. The app services in our area charge about $140.
- Our cleaners are employees, not contractors. We pay $21 an hour and carry insurance on every visit.
- Last year 7 of our 18 cleaners left, so about 4 in 10 customers had their regular cleaner change at least once.
- We now give each customer a regular cleaner and a named backup.
- Returning customers get their first cleaning for $99.

I want the email to promise that you'll get the same cleaner every single time. Keep it to about 150 words.

Before I draft this, there's one thing I need to raise, plus a few questions.

**The promise.** Your own setup gives each customer a regular cleaner *and a named backup*. So "the same cleaner every single time" isn't what you actually offer, and with 7 of 18 cleaners leaving last year, some customers will see a change again. These are people who left partly over this exact issue. If you break the promise a second time, they're unlikely to come back again. I'd suggest "your own regular cleaner, plus one named backup you'll know by name, never a stranger." That's still a strong promise, and it's one you can keep.

A few questions:

1. **Can you go with the "regular cleaner + named backup" wording?** If you really can guarantee one person every time (for example, by skipping a visit rather than sending the backup), tell me how that works and I'll write it that way.
2. **Does the $99 offer have a deadline or any conditions?** For example, does it need a recurring booking, or is it only for a 3-bedroom?
3. **How should they rebook?** A link, a phone number, or just replying to the email?
4. **Should I address price directly?** I could say you're $25 more than the apps because your cleaners are insured employees paid $21 an hour, or I could just lead with the $99 offer and leave price out.
5. **Who signs it?** Your name and title, and the company name.

1. Yes, use that. I can't promise the same cleaner every time because of sick days and holidays, but make it as strong as you can without saying anything false.
2. It ends December 31. I don't know of any other conditions.
3. They can reply to the email or call 555-0164.
4. Whichever you think works better. I can't match $140. If you mention price, most of the app services here use contractors with no insurance on the visit.
5. Lisa Grant, Owner, Brightway Home Cleaning.

<final_document>
Subject: You told us what went wrong. We've fixed it.

Hi [First name],

When you cancelled, you told us what went wrong. Two answers came up most often: price, and a different cleaner at the door each time.

We've fixed the second one. Every customer now has their own regular cleaner, plus one named backup for sick days and holidays. You'll know them both by name.

About price: we do cost more than the app services. Here's why. Our cleaners are employees paid $21 an hour, and every visit is insured. Most app services in our area use contractors, with no insurance on the visit.

To make coming back easy, your first cleaning is $99. This offer ends December 31.

Just reply to this email or call 555-0164, and we'll match you with your regular cleaner.

Lisa Grant
Owner, Brightway Home Cleaning
</final_document>

The email is about 140 words. A few notes:

- **Cleaner wording:** I said "your own regular cleaner, plus one named backup" and avoided "never a stranger." On a day when both are out, a third person might show up, and that line would turn out to be false.
- **Why I mentioned price:** Price was the top reason people left, so I addressed it. Saying it outright and explaining why you cost more comes across better than staying quiet about it. The contractor and insurance line is based on what you told me. Check that it's accurate before you send.
- **A detail to settle first:** The email says nothing about whether the $99 cleaning requires going back on a regular schedule. If you'd want that, add it now. That's easier than turning down someone who books just one cleaning.
